astrŏlŏgus , i, m., = ἀστρολόγος.
I. An astronomer (class. for the later astronomus; v. the preced. art.), Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 7; 2, 3, 7; Cic. Div. 2, 42, 87; “and in a pun: (Verres) novus astrologus, qui non tam caeli rationem quam caelati argenti duceret, etc.,” Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 52 .—
II. A star-interpreter, astrologer: “Astrologorum signa in caelo quaesit, observat,” Enn. Trag. Rel. p. 42 Rib.; Cic. Div. 1, 58, 132; 1, 6, 12; 1, 39, 85; id. Fam. 6, 6; Juv. 6, 554; Suet. Ner. 36.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
